title: Part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks: the picks define the full 3D frame
body:
# Part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks: the picks define the full 3D frame

## What

The axis-pick panel (Setup > align) refuses an out-of-plane pick: "the
+Y pick runs (nearly) along the work plane's normal (Z)". But two
perpendicular picks — an edge for +X, an edge for +Y — already define a
complete 3D frame: the +X pick's direction maps to world +X, the +Y
pick's to world +Y, and Z+ follows by the right-hand rule (the user's
rule: the directions decide where Z+ points). Today's `turn_in_plane`
(`app/src/pick/axis.rs`) only spins about the work plane's normal and
throws that information away.

## The law (from the discussion with the user)

- Pick two lines (edges or two-point picks) that run across each
  other: the +X pick's direction maps to world +X, the +Y pick's to
  world +Y, and the part's Z+ lands where the right-hand rule puts it
  (R(d_x) x R(d_y) = +Z).
- The pivot is the parts' centre (the part stays on its spot of the
  table) — the ORIGIN question is deliberately out of scope here: the
  work offset is placed separately, as it is today.
- Nearly-perpendicular picks: the primary axis lands exactly, the
  secondary is orthogonalized against it; picks that run (nearly)
  along each other refuse by name (no frame can be read from them).
- Flip flags keep their meaning (a reversed edge flips its direction).
- The landing is proven before the command stores anything (the
  primary runs along its axis, the secondary within the skew it came
  with, the frame right-handed) — never a silently wrong frame.

## Scope

- `pick/axis.rs`: `align_from_axes(world, setup, axes)` — the general
  construction, which subsumes the in-plane turn for in-plane picks.
- `commands/setup_align.rs`: the `AlignPartToSetup` constructor for it.
- The UI call site (`ui/src/state.rs`, the axis-pick panel's apply)
  switches from `turn_in_plane` to the general path — the same panel,
  the same picks, now with the full meaning.
- `turn_in_plane` stays for its in-plane callers; the general path must
  reproduce its results for in-plane picks (subsumption, pinned
  numerically).

## Done means

- The user's exact case aligns: a part whose +Y edge runs along world
  (0, 0, -1) and +X edge along (-1, 0, 0) lands with +Y along +Y, +X
  along +X and the cross-normal up — one pick round, no plane-first
  step.
- In-plane picks behave exactly as `turn_in_plane` did (existing suites
  green: turn_pivot, plane_align, the setup axis tests).
- Numeric tests: out-of-plane perpendicular picks, subsumption for
  in-plane picks, near-perpendicular skew, parallel picks refused by
  name, flips honored, undo restores.
